intro: Rhode Island runs its elections through the State Board of Elections and a local board of canvassers in each city and town.

id_rule.text: Bring a photo ID to vote at the polls. Accepted IDs include a Rhode Island driver's license or permit, a Rhode Island voter ID card, a U.S. passport, a school ID from a U.S. educational institution, a U.S. military ID, a government-issued ID or medical card, or a tribal ID. If you can't show one, you vote a provisional ballot. You don't need ID to vote by mail ballot.

elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: You must be registered 30 days before the election to vote at the polls. This date falls on a Sunday.

dates.label: Mail ballot application deadline
dates.detail: Apply for a mail ballot by this date. No reason is needed. Emergency mail ballot applications are accepted until 4 pm on Nov. 2.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Registered voters can vote early in person during the 20 days before Election Day, at their city or town hall or another site set by the local board of canvassers. Check your local board for days and hours.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm, except New Shoreham, which opens at 9 am. A mail ballot must be received by the State Board of Elections by 8 pm. You can use an official drop box if it is too late to mail it.
